The agent asked the caller for a specific piece of information (a name, a number, a date, a choice) that the caller had already stated earlier in the call. A caller who repeats a request does not count, and neither does an agent that reads details back to have them confirmed. Quote the agent's question, and give as earlier_turn the turn in which the caller had stated that information.

The agent told the caller that it did or recorded something (booked, sent, saved, noted, remembered, cancelled, changed) although no tool call that ran and succeeded did it. The agent can do and record things only through its tools. So when a tool in the list is how that is done and no call of it ran and succeeded, the claim is unbacked, and so it is when the list holds no tool for it at all. Saying back what the caller said, or what it is going to do, is not such a claim. Quote the agent's claim.
The agent ignored or misread something the caller said. Quote the agent's reply that shows it.
The agent repeated itself, contradicted itself, or said something that does not follow from the call. Quote the agent's words.
The agent's tool calls did not match what the caller asked for, or came in an order that makes no sense. Quote the tool call, or the agent's words about it.

The agent ended the call although the caller had not said goodbye and had not said that they needed nothing else. Having done what the caller last asked for is no reason to end the call. When the caller did say goodbye, an earlier request of theirs that went unanswered is not this finding: that is ignored_caller. Answer no when the agent did not end the call. Quote the last words before the call ended.
The agent reads the booking back.

The agent asked the caller for a specific piece of information (a name, a number, a date, a choice) that the caller had already stated earlier in the call. A caller who repeats a request does not count, and neither does an agent that reads details back to have them confirmed. Quote the agent's question, and give as earlier_turn the turn in which the caller had stated that information.

The agent told the caller that it did or recorded something (booked, sent, saved, noted, remembered, cancelled, changed) although no tool call that ran and succeeded did it. The agent can do and record things only through its tools. So when a tool in the list is how that is done and no call of it ran and succeeded, the claim is unbacked, and so it is when the list holds no tool for it at all. Saying back what the caller said, or what it is going to do, is not such a claim. Quote the agent's claim.
The agent ignored or misread something the caller said. Quote the agent's reply that shows it.
The agent repeated itself, contradicted itself, or said something that does not follow from the call. Quote the agent's words.
The agent's tool calls did not match what the caller asked for, or came in an order that makes no sense. Quote the tool call, or the agent's words about it.

The agent ended the call although the caller had not said goodbye and had not said that they needed nothing else. Having done what the caller last asked for is no reason to end the call. When the caller did say goodbye, an earlier request of theirs that went unanswered is not this finding: that is ignored_caller. Answer no when the agent did not end the call. Quote the last words before the call ended.
